name: LANE_OUTPUT_SIGNAL_PARSES_LQ1691_20261109
comment: "path": "logs/watch_outcomes.log"}. observe_signal reads a json_key signal with json.loads over the whole
file; the declared path is a plain-text cron log, so the read raises JSONDecodeError and the signal is
readable: false for every run. The supervisor grades an unreadable signal as NO_OUTPUT, so no green run
could ever clear the breach: 3 OPEN NO_OUTPUT breaches (11-07/08/09) in a 2,766-row breach log, and this
is the only one of 723 lanes with the defect.
This gate pins the fix: the signal names the LaneRunReceipt the lane actually writes
not by hand), the allowlist agrees, the health contract's receipt/verify/expected_output evidence name it,
and observe_signal over that receipt is readable both with ok_at set (green run clears the breach) and
ok_at null (a failed run is silent, not unreadable). A registry-wide rule keeps a json_key signal off any
non-JSON path, so the class cannot return.
Hermetic: config files are read as text and observe_signal runs against a temporary root; no live
artifact, ledger, database, network or clock read.
